put.summary: Create or update a secret set
put.description:
Create a new secret set or update an existing one. Supports both regular secrets (multiple key-value pairs) and image pull secrets.

Provisioning is **asynchronous**: the response is `202 Accepted` once the values have been stored, and the secret set is then provisioned into the target region in the background. Use `GET /secrets/{setName}` to observe the readiness status (`pending` → `ready`). Deploys that bind a secret set whose status is not `ready` are rejected with `409 Conflict`.

parameters.name: setName
parameters.description: Name of the secret set to create or update

regularSecrets.description: Create or update a set with multiple key-value pairs

imagePullSecret.description: Create or update an image pull secret

202.description: Secret set accepted. Values have been stored and the set is being provisioned into the target region in the background. Poll `GET /secrets/{setName}` until `status` is `ready` before binding it to a deploy.

region.description: The region where the secret set was created or exists

Cannot update existing regular secrets to image pull secrets

Invalid request format

put.summary: Link an environment to a project
put.description:
Links `agentName` as an environment of `parent`. An environment is an agent of its own, with its own repository binding, secrets and scaling; the link only records that it belongs to the project.

This sets the whole link, so it also renames an environment or moves it to another project, and every rule is checked again either way.

The link is refused when the two agents are in different regions, when either side already has environments (environments do not nest), when the project has PR previews on, when the name is already taken by another of the project's environments, or when `agentName` is a PR preview, whose link belongs to its pull request.

parameters.name: agentName
parameters.description: Name of the agent to link as an environment

parent.description: Name of the project the environment belongs to

environmentName.description: Its name among the project's environments: two to 50 lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending with a letter or digit. `production` is the project itself, and the `pr-` prefix is reserved for PR previews.

parent.description: The project it belongs to, or null when unlinked

environmentName.description: Its name among the project's environments, or null when unlinked

400.description: A reserved or malformed environment name, a region mismatch, or an agent asked to be an environment of itself

example.error: An agent cannot be an environment of itself

404.description: The agent or the parent was not found

409.description: Environments would nest, the name is taken, the project has PR previews on, or the agent is a PR preview

delete.description:
Removes the link between an environment and its project. The agent stays, running as before, and becomes a project of its own; the project's watch paths it had been following become its own, so it goes on deploying as it did.

Idempotent: an agent that is not an environment answers 200. A PR preview cannot be unlinked, since its link belongs to its pull request.

parameters.name: agentName
parameters.description: Name of the environment's agent

200.description: The agent is no longer an environment

parent.description: The project it belongs to, or null when unlinked

environmentName.description: Its name among the project's environments, or null when unlinked

404.description: Agent not found

409.description: The agent is a PR preview, whose link is managed by its pull request

example.error: A PR preview's link is managed by its pull request

put.description:
Turns PR previews on for a project with the secret set they mount, or off with `null`.

Choosing the set is what turns previews on: every same-repo pull request into the branch the project deploys from then becomes an environment named `pr-<number>`, built from the pull request's head and scaled to at most one instance. A preview mounts only this set, never the project's own, and a pull request touching none of the project's watch paths gets no preview.

`null` turns previews off and the previews that exist are deleted within minutes. Turning them off always succeeds, whatever state the project is in.

Turning them on needs a GitHub repository connected to the project, a secret set that exists in the project's region and is ready to mount, and an organization that is not suspended. An agent that is itself an environment cannot have previews.

parameters.name: agentName
parameters.description: Name of the project

secretSet.description: Secret set every preview mounts, or null to turn previews off

botPullRequests.description: Whether pull requests opened by bots (Dependabot, Renovate, GitHub Apps) get previews too. Left out, the stored setting is kept.

secretSet.description: The secret set previews mount, or null when previews are off

botPullRequests.description: Whether bot pull requests get previews

400.description: No GitHub repository is connected, or the secret set is in another region

example.error: PR previews need a GitHub repository connected to this agent

404.description: The agent or the secret set was not found

409.description: The agent is an environment of another agent, or the secret set is not ready to mount

example.error: An environment of another agent cannot have PR previews

put.description:
Sets the glob patterns a change has to match for a push to deploy the project, or for a pull request to get a PR preview. An empty array clears them, so every change deploys.

Watch paths are a project setting: the project, its environments and its PR previews all follow this one list, so setting them on an environment is refused. The project needs a GitHub repository connected.

Patterns are relative to the repository root. A leading `!` excludes and the last pattern a file matches decides, so a list of only exclusions is refused. `**` is allowed as a whole path level at most twice, and at most one `*` between slashes; `?` and braces are refused. A pattern that matches a folder also matches everything in it, and a trailing `/` is refused. The `Dockerfile` and `.dockerignore` always count as watched.

parameters.name: agentName
parameters.description: Name of the project

watchPaths.description: Glob patterns a change must match to deploy. An empty array clears them.

400.description: A malformed pattern, too many patterns, or no GitHub repository connected

example.error: Watch paths need a GitHub repository connected to this agent

404.description: Agent not found

409.description: The agent is an environment of another agent

example.error: An environment of another agent follows its project's watch paths; set them on the project

post.description:
Checks the scenario, then queues an eval run against the agent. A `synthetic` run holds its own conversation with a new session of the agent. A `session` run judges one of the agent's sessions that has ended, and starts no session. Poll the run until its `result` is set.

The run's files are the request's own (`files`), or a revision of one of the organization's bundles (`bundleRevisionId`), never both. Inline files are kept as an anonymous revision that only this run names: the run's `bundleRevisionId` reads them back. A request that names a revision takes a `requestId`. Sending the same request again with the same `requestId` answers `202` with the run as it is now and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and creates nothing; the same `requestId` with a different request is a `409`. A refused request records nothing, its `requestId` included.

A synthetic run calls the agent's real tools. See the [Evals guide](/pipecat-cloud/guides/evals).

Organizations with HIPAA controls cannot create runs. Controls are checked again before starting a synthetic session or a session judge. Enabling controls prevents further starts; evaluations already in progress continue. Runs can still be read, listed and cancelled.

files.greeting.yaml:
name: greeting
scenarios:
  - name: capital_question
    turns:
      - user: "What is the capital of France?"
        expect:
          - event: response
            eval: "the response says the capital of France is Paris"

202.description: The run, queued; or, replayed, the run an earlier request with this `requestId` made, as it is now.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before polling. Sent while the run is live.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when an earlier request with this `requestId` made the run.

400.description: The body is invalid (`err.issues` says where), the deadline is too short, a session run has no `sessionId`, has `params` or has a `measure:` metric, a synthetic run has a `sessionId`, the request has both or neither of `files` and `bundleRevisionId`, a `bundleRevisionId` comes without a `requestId`, `scenarioPath` isn't one of the run's files, the scenario can't run (`error` gives the reasons), the agent's region has no hosted evals, or, for a session run, judging sessions isn't available in the agent's region yet.

403.description: The organization is suspended (code `PCC-1007`), or has HIPAA controls (`Hosted evals aren't available for organizations with HIPAA controls.`). Hosted evals are refused for both kinds of run.

404.description: The organization has no agent of this name (`Agent not found`); a session run's `sessionId` is not a session of this agent (`Session not found`); or the organization has no bundle revision with this `bundleRevisionId` (`Eval bundle revision not found`), an anonymous revision and one removed after its bundle was deleted included.

409.description: A session run's session hasn't ended yet, so its conversation hasn't been published. A session that ended because the platform stopped hearing from it can't be judged until 5 hours after it was created; `error` gives that time. The named revision's bundle has been deleted (code `EVAL-BUNDLE-DELETED`). Or the `requestId` was already used for a different request (code `EVAL-REQUEST-ID-CONFLICT`).

413.description: The files hold more than 256 KiB in all, take more than 3.5 MiB as JSON, or the request is more than 3 MiB.

415.description: The request is in another charset than UTF-8.

500.description: Evals are misconfigured on our side. Retrying won't help.

503.description: Evals are not enabled here (code `EVALS-NOT-AVAILABLE`, no `Retry-After`), or the scenario couldn't be checked right now (retry after the `Retry-After` header).

parameters.name: suiteRunId

400.description: A query parameter is invalid: `limit` or `offset` out of range, an unknown `kind`, `status` or `verdict`, or a `suiteRunId` that isn't a UUID (`err.issues` says which).

404.description: The organization has no agent of this name.

get.description: Returns the run. While it is live, `result` is null and the `Retry-After` header says when to poll again.

400.description: `runId` is not a UUID (`err.issues` says so).

404.description: The organization has no agent of this name, or the agent has no run with this ID.

post.description: Requests cancellation and returns the run's current state. Takes no body: send none, or send `{}` with `Content-Type: application/json`. A queued run ends at once as `cancelled`. A run that has started may still be `starting` or `running` in the response. No further cancel request is needed; optionally GET the run to check its eventual outcome. Stopping an active evaluation is best effort: `cancelled` does not confirm that all evaluation activity has stopped. If stopping could not be confirmed, `result.reason` says the evaluation may continue until its deadline. Cancellation does not undo usage already incurred by an agent session. A run that reaches its own end before the cancel does keeps that end. Cancelling a cancelled run is safe. Allowed while the organization is suspended.

200.description: The cancellation request was recorded, or the run was already cancelled. Returns the current run, which may still be `starting` or `running`, or may already be `cancelled`. No `Retry-After` or `Location` header is sent.

400.description: `runId` is not a UUID, or the request has a body other than an empty JSON object sent with `Content-Type: application/json`.

404.description: The organization has no agent of this name, or the agent has no run with this ID.

409.description: The run has already finished another way (`The run has already finished.`). It is left as it ended.

413.description: The JSON or form body exceeds the request body size limit.

415.description: A JSON or form body declares an unsupported charset or Content-Encoding.

get.description: Read-only discovery of what hosted evals offer the organization, readable even when hosted evals are off. `enabled` is whether hosted evals are on. `creation` says whether the organization may create runs and publish bundles. `bundles` and `suites` say whether stored bundles and suite runs are available. Every answer is advisory: a run, a suite run or a publication is still checked when it is submitted.

200.description: Discovery succeeded, including when evals are off or restricted.

404.description: Organization not found.

get.description: Read-only discovery of the kinds of run an agent can have: `synthetic`, with `synthetic.audio` for audio scenarios, and `session`. Each kind's `state` is `available`, `unavailable` or `unknown`, which means availability couldn't be established right now. Discovery starts no session and reads no conversation, and `available` doesn't promise that a particular run will succeed: a run is still checked when it is created. Use this for one agent you're about to run; for lists, use the organization's capabilities.

200.description: Availability, including disabled, restricted and unknown states.

audio.message: Audio evals aren't available for agents in this region yet.

404.description: The organization, or a live agent of this name in it, was not found.

post.description: Checks every file of the bundle, then creates the bundle and its revision 1 together. Nothing is recorded unless the answer is `201`, the `requestId` included. Sending the same request again with the same `requestId` answers as the first did, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same `requestId` with a different request is a `409`. A `requestId` lasts as long as the revision it made. Organizations that are suspended or have HIPAA controls cannot publish.

files.suite.yaml:
kind: suite
schemaVersion: 1
suite:
  - name: baseline
    scenarios:
      - greet.yaml
files.greet.yaml:
name: greet
scenarios:
  - name: hello
    persona: "A caller who says hello and asks the agent its name."
    goal: "Learn what the agent is called, then end the call."
    success: "the agent answered the caller and the conversation ended politely"

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when an earlier request with this `requestId` made the bundle.

409.description: A bundle of the organization already has this name (code `EVAL-BUNDLE-NAME-TAKEN`), or the `requestId` was already used for a different request (code `EVAL-REQUEST-ID-CONFLICT`).

415.description: The request is in another charset than UTF-8.

500.description: Bundle checks are misconfigured on our side. Retrying won't help.

get.description: Returns a bundle and its latest revision.

delete.description: Takes the bundle out of the catalog: it is no longer listed, read or appended to, and its name can be taken by a new bundle, with a new ID, starting at revision 1. Its revisions that runs name stay readable by ID while those runs are kept; the rest are removed soon after. Runs already accepted are unaffected, but no new run can name its revisions. Open to suspended organizations and those with HIPAA controls.

400.description: `bundleId` is not a UUID (`err.issues` says so).

404.description: The organization has no bundle with this ID, one already deleted included.

post.description: Checks every file, then adds them as the bundle's next revision, numbered one more than its latest. Identical files make a new revision too. Retries with a `requestId`, and the restrictions on publishing, are as for [creating a bundle](/api-reference/pipecat-cloud/rest-reference/endpoint/eval-bundle-create).

201.description: The new revision, without its files.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when an earlier request with this `requestId` made the revision.

404.description: The organization has no bundle with this ID, one deleted meanwhile included.

409.description: The `requestId` was already used for a different request (code `EVAL-REQUEST-ID-CONFLICT`).

415.description: The request is in another charset than UTF-8.

500.description: Bundle checks are misconfigured on our side. Retrying won't help.

get.description: Returns a bundle's revisions, newest first, without their files.

200.description: A page of revisions. `total_count` counts them all.

404.description: The organization has no bundle with this ID.

get.description: Returns a revision with its files exactly as they were received, a catalog of what they hold, their digest and what checked them. A deleted bundle's revisions that runs name are read here too, and so are the anonymous revisions that inline files are kept as.

400.description: `revisionId` is not a UUID (`err.issues` says so).

404.description: The organization has no revision with this ID.

post.description:
Plans a suite run, checks every scenario it selects in the agent's region, and accepts it with its plan: every member it will run, in order. Each member runs as an eval run of its own, which holds its result. Poll the suite run until it has ended.

The files are a stored revision (`bundleRevisionId`) or the request's own (`files`), which are checked as a bundle and kept as an anonymous revision that only this suite run names. The suite run runs a suite file (`suitePath`), or the scenarios of one scenario file (`scenarioPath`, narrowed by `scenarioNames`).

Nothing is recorded unless the answer is `202`. Sending the same request again with the same `requestId` answers as the first did, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same `requestId` with a different request is a `409`. Organizations that are suspended or have HIPAA controls cannot run suites.

Every member starts a real session of the agent, which calls its real tools. See the [Evals guide](/pipecat-cloud/guides/evals#run-a-suite).

202.description: The suite run, accepted, with its plan. Its members are at its `items`.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when an earlier request with this `requestId` made the suite run.

400.description: The body is invalid (`err.issues` says where); inline files the check refused (code `EVAL-BUNDLE-REFUSED`, with `problems` and `total`); a filter naming one scenario twice; a plan that can't be made (code `EVAL-SUITE-PLAN-INVALID`, with `refusal`); scenarios the agent's region would refuse (code `EVAL-SUITE-SCENARIOS-REFUSED`, with `problems` and `total`); an entry body larger than a session's body may be, or entry bodies for an agent not deployed with `websocket_auth = "token"`; or an agent in a region without hosted evals.

404.description: The organization has no agent of this name, or no bundle revision with this `bundleRevisionId`, an anonymous revision and one removed after its bundle was deleted included.

409.description: The revision's bundle has been deleted (code `EVAL-BUNDLE-DELETED`); the `requestId` was already used for a different request (code `EVAL-REQUEST-ID-CONFLICT`); or the agent is between deployments (code `EVAL-AGENT-BETWEEN-DEPLOYMENTS`). A suite run's members are held to the deployment the agent is on when it is accepted, so retry once the deployment has completed. Only the last of these clears on a retry.

413.description: Inline files larger than a bundle may hold, or whose contents are too large to catalogue.

503.description: The suite run couldn't be checked right now (code `503`; retry after the `Retry-After` header). Or, with no `Retry-After`: suite runs aren't available here or in the agent's region (code `EVAL-SUITES-NOT-AVAILABLE`), inline files can't be checked here (code `EVAL-BUNDLES-NOT-AVAILABLE`), or hosted evals aren't enabled (code `EVALS-NOT-AVAILABLE`).

get.description: Returns the suite run with its plan, its members' counts, its verdict once it has completed, and a measurement's pass rates. While it hasn't ended, the `Retry-After` header says when to poll again.

404.description: The organization has no suite run with this ID.

post.description: Requests cancellation and returns the suite run's current state. Takes no body: send none, or send `{}` with `Content-Type: application/json`. Once the request is recorded, the suite run admits no more members, its members not yet admitted end without running, and its live members are cancelled as a [cancelled eval run](/api-reference/pipecat-cloud/rest-reference/endpoint/eval-run-cancel) is. It may still be `running` in the response while they finish; results they reach first are kept. It then ends `cancelled`, unless something else had already stopped it, such as its deadline, whose end it keeps. Cancelling again is safe. Allowed while the organization is suspended.

200.description: The cancellation request is recorded, or one already was, however the suite run then ended. Returns the current suite run, with a `Retry-After` header while it hasn't ended.

400.description: The request has a body other than an empty JSON object sent with `Content-Type: application/json`.

404.description: The organization has no suite run with this ID.

409.description: The suite run had already ended, with no cancel requested (`The suite run has already finished.`). It is left as it ended.

get.description: Returns every planned member in plan order, a page at a time, each with its eval run's ID once it has been admitted. Read a member's result from its eval run, or list them all with the eval run list's `suiteRunId` filter.

404.description: The organization has no suite run with this ID.

PrivateKeyAuth.description:
Authentication requires a Pipecat Cloud Private API token.

Generate a Private API key from your Dashboard (Settings > API Keys > Private > Create key) and include it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

BearerAuth.description: Authentication using a Pipecat Cloud API token.

PublicKeyAuth.description:
Authentication using a Pipecat Cloud public API key.

Generate a public API key from your Dashboard (Settings > API Keys > Public > Create key) and include it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

PersonalAccessTokenAuth.description: A personal access token (`pcc_pat_...`) of a member of the organization, or the CLI's OAuth token. See [Personal Access Tokens](/pipecat-cloud/guides/personal-access-tokens).

serviceName.description:
Name of the agent to create.

Must start with a lowercase letter or number, can include hyphens, and must end with a lowercase letter or number. No uppercase letters or special characters allowed. Maximum 54 characters.

image.description: The container image to use for the agent. Either `image` or `buildId` must be provided, but not both.

buildId.description: The ID of a successful cloud build to deploy. Either `image` or `buildId` must be provided, but not both. The build must be in the same region as the agent.

region.description: The region where the agent will be deployed. If not specified, defaults to `us-west`. All secrets and image pull secrets referenced by this agent must be in the same region.

architecture.description: Target CPU architecture for the agent's containers: `amd64` or `arm64`. Must be one of the architectures the target region supports (see the `supported_architectures` field on [List available regions](#tag/Regions)). If omitted, the region's default architecture is used. Daily-hosted regions currently support `arm64` only. Set this explicitly when your image is built for a single architecture so it schedules on matching nodes instead of failing at startup.

nodeType.description: Deprecated: use `architecture` instead. Legacy alias where `arm` maps to `arm64` and `amd` maps to `amd64`. Ignored when `architecture` is present.

imagePullSecretSet.description: The name of the image pull secret set to use. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, to create the agent with no image pull secret set.

secretSet.description: The name of the secret set to use. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, to create the agent with no secret set.

krispViva.description: Krisp VIVA noise cancellation configuration. [Learn more](/pipecat-cloud/guides/krisp-viva).

audioFilter.description:
The Krisp VIVA audio filter model to use:

- `tel`: Optimized for telephony, cellular, landline, mobile, desktop, and browser (up to 16kHz)
- `pro`: Optimized for mobile, desktop, and browser with WebRTC (up to 32kHz)
- `null`: Disables Krisp VIVA

By default, Pipecat processes input audio at 16kHz, making `tel` appropriate for most use cases.

agentProfile.description:
The agent profile to use for resource allocation. Valid values are:

- `agent-1x`: 0.5 vCPU and 1 GB of memory. Best for voice agents.
- `agent-2x`: 1 vCPU and 2 GB of memory. Well suited for voice and video agents or voice agents requiring extra processing.
- `agent-3x`: 1.5 vCPU and 3 GB of memory. Best for voice and video agents requiring extra processing or multiple video inputs.

In a self-hosted region, this may also name one of your organization's own profiles, or be omitted in favour of `resources`.

resources.description: Explicit sizing for agents in self-hosted regions, using Kubernetes quantities (e.g. `cpu: "1"`, `memory: "2Gi"`). Mutually exclusive with `agentProfile`; accepted only when the target region is self-hosted.

maxSessionDuration.description: Maximum session duration in seconds. When a session reaches this limit, the session is stopped: the bot is cancelled, with no opportunity for it to say goodbye first. Valid range: 60 to 14400 (4 hours). Defaults to 7200 (2 hours) when unset.

err.description: On a `400` for a body or parameter that failed validation: `issues`, each with the `path` of what failed and a `message` saying why.

createDailyRoom.description: Whether to create a Daily room for the service instance

dailyRoomProperties.description:
Optional configuration for the Daily room. Only used when createDailyRoom is true.

See [Daily API documentation](https://docs.daily.co/reference/rest-api/rooms/config) for supported properties.

dailyMeetingTokenProperties.description:
Optional configuration for the Daily meeting token. Only used when createDailyRoom is true.

See [Daily API documentation](https://docs.daily.co/reference/rest-api/meeting-tokens/config) for supported properties.

enableDefaultIceServers.description: Whether to use the default STUN/TURN ICE servers provided by Pipecat Cloud.

transport.description: Explicitly specify which transport the bot should use. `moq` starts a Media over QUIC session: the response's `moq` field carries what the browser transport needs, and `createDailyRoom` and `enableDefaultIceServers` cannot be set to `true` with it. Around a deploy, a `moq` start can get `409 Conflict`; see the 409 response. See the [Media over QUIC guide](/pipecat-cloud/guides/moq).

body.description: Arbitrary user data / configuration object to pass to the service instance. Accessible as the first parameter of the `bot` method or custom entry point. Maximum size: 1 MB for `transport: "daily"`, `"webrtc"` or `"moq"`, 4 KB for `"websocket"`. For `transport: "websocket"`, the body is returned in the response's `body` field base64-encoded; the service must be deployed with `websocket_auth = "token"` to use this encoding convenience. See the [`Starting Sessions` docs](/pipecat-cloud/fundamentals/active-sessions#passing-data) for details.

token.description: HMAC session token for WebSocket authentication (only when transport is "websocket")

wsUrl.description: WebSocket URL to connect to (only when transport is "websocket")

body.description: Base64-encoded JSON body for the bot (only when transport is "websocket" and the request included a `body`). URL-encode it and append it to `wsUrl` as the `?body=` query parameter when connecting.

dailyRoom.description: URL of the created Daily room (if createDailyRoom was set to true)

dailyToken.description: Token to access the Daily room (if createDailyRoom was set to true)

sessionId.description: Session ID for the created session

moq.description: What `@pipecat-ai/moq-transport` needs to join the session (only when transport is "moq"). Pass the whole response to the transport's `connect()`, which `startBotAndConnect()` does for you, and the transport reads this field itself. See the [Media over QUIC guide](/pipecat-cloud/guides/moq).

relayUrl.description: The URL of the MoQ relays in the agent's region, with the browser's credential for this session in its query string. Treat it as a secret.

certHash.description: Always null: the relays use publicly trusted certificates, so there is no certificate to pin.

namespace.description: The session's namespace. The browser publishes under `<namespace>/<clientId>` and subscribes to `<namespace>/<botId>`.

transcriptTrack.description: The name of the track, on each side's broadcast, that carries that side's RTVI messages.

iceConfig.description: ICE server configuration (only included when enableDefaultIceServers is true)

session_id.description: Session ID of the stopped session

EvalRunRequest.description: A run's request: its files inline (`files`), or a stored revision of one of the organization's bundles (`bundleRevisionId`) with a `requestId`. Exactly one of `files` and `bundleRevisionId`.

kind.description: `synthetic` holds a new conversation with the agent. `session` judges an ended session of the agent by the scenario's `success:` and `metrics:`, and takes no `params`.

sessionId.description: A session run's session: one of the agent's that has ended. The agent must publish its conversations (`PCC_EVAL_CONVERSATIONS=true`), or the run ends `not_started`. Not allowed on a synthetic run.

files.description: Every file the scenario may include, keyed by path relative to the bundle's root, with UTF-8 text values. At least one file, at most 256 KiB in all, at most 3.5 MiB as JSON with paths counted. Paths are at most 1024 characters. The files are kept as an anonymous revision, which the run's `bundleRevisionId` names.

scenarioPath.description: The scenario's file: one of the keys of `files`.

scenarioName.description: The scenario's name within its file.

deadlineSeconds.description: How long the run may take from its creation, queueing included. A run still going then ends as `expired`. A session run takes 240 to 1800 seconds, and defaults to 600.

requestId.description: A UUID you generate for this request and send again, unchanged, when you retry it. Unique in the organization among runs that name a revision, and kept as long as the run it made.

bundleRevisionId.description: A revision of one of the organization's bundles, whose files the run runs, while the bundle hasn't been deleted. [Get an eval bundle](/api-reference/pipecat-cloud/rest-reference/endpoint/eval-bundle-get) gives its latest revision's ID. An anonymous revision belongs to its own run, and naming one is a `404`.

scenarioPath.description: The scenario's file: one of the revision's files.

scenarioName.description: The scenario's name within its file.

defaultTimeoutMs.description: How long a turn waits for the agent by default.

total_count.description: How many runs match, before pagination.

serviceName.description: The run's agent. Null when the agent has since been deleted.

environmentName.description: The agent's environment label, as it is now. Null for an agent that isn't an environment of another.

parentServiceName.description: The parent agent's name, set together with `environmentName`.

verdict.description: Set only on a completed run.

bundleRevisionId.description: The bundle revision whose files the run runs, which [Get an eval bundle revision](/api-reference/pipecat-cloud/rest-reference/endpoint/eval-bundle-revision-get) reads: the one its request named, or the anonymous revision its inline files were kept as. Null on a run created before runs were kept with a revision.

suiteRunId.description: The suite run it is a member of. Null for a run of its own.

suiteMemberOrdinal.description: Its place in its suite run's plan, from 0. Null for a run of its own.

executor.description: What judged the run: its judging version (`fingerprint`), which identifies everything that decides a verdict, and the build of the eval service that ran it (`build`). Null until they are reported.

sessionId.description: The agent session associated with the run, if one is known. A session run's is the session it judges.

startedAt.description: When the run first left the queue. Null on a run that ended without leaving it.

reason.description: The verdict's reason, or why the run has none.

conversation.description: The conversation, in Pipecat's format. In a scripted run, the assistant messages are the agent's LLM output, or its recognized speech when judging audio, and the user messages are the script's wording as sent, which doesn't confirm the agent received it; a scripted run's conversation can be empty. A run that failed can keep the conversation so far. Empty when `truncated` is `true`.

ignored.description: The scenario's keys that had no effect, the first 20 of them.

truncated.description: The result was too large to keep whole, so its conversation, details and metric reasons were left out.

EvalRunResult.description: Null while the run is live; an ended run's result otherwise.

EvalRunDetails.description: A run's turns, failures and goal. Reasons, and what a check matched, are the judge's and Pipecat's words, and quote the conversation. Null when the run reached no result, when the result was too large to keep whole (`truncated`), or when it couldn't be read.

kind.description: `script`: a scenario of scripted turns. `simulation`: a persona's conversation with the agent.

turns.description: In order. A scripted scenario's turns are all of its own; a simulation's are the agent's turns its judged metrics were asked about, so none when it has no judged metrics.

failures.description: What made the run fall short: a scripted scenario's failed checks and turns; a simulation's goal when the judge found it not met (first), then its judged metrics on each turn they failed, or a measured metric's for the whole run.

turn.description: The first is 1. A scripted scenario's turn is its own: what it sends and the agent's reply. A simulation's counts the agent's turns in `conversation`.

speaker.description: Whose turns `turn` counts: `agent` on a simulation; null on a scripted scenario, whose turns are the scenario's.

status.description: `not_run`: the scripted run stopped before this turn.

reason.description: Why the whole turn failed, apart from its checks, such as a scripted turn's input that was never sent. Null otherwise.

checks.description: What each check found on the turn, in the scenario's order. A scripted turn's checks end at the first that timed out.

name.description: A scripted check's expected event, or a simulation's metric name.

verdict.description: The judge's answer on a simulation's turn: `none` when it gave none, which fails the check. Null on a scripted check.

reason.description: Why a scripted check failed, or the judge's reason on a simulation's turn. Null for a scripted check that passed.

matched.description: What a scripted check that passed matched, such as the agent's reply. Null otherwise.

kind.description: How it failed, as Pipecat names it, for grouping across runs: `timeout`, `text_mismatch`, `judge_no`, `connect_failed` and others. `judge_no_verdict`: the judge gave no verdict, a failed call to it included. `goal_not_met`: a simulation's goal the judge found not met. `audio_unsupported`: the agent's eval transport has audio turned off that the scenario uses, so the conversation never started. New kinds may appear.

turn.description: The turn it happened on, numbered as in `turns`. Null for a failure of the whole run, such as a failed connection or a measured metric.

name.description: The failed check's name, as in `turns`. Null for a failure of a whole turn or run.

EvalRunGoal.description: A simulation's goal. Null for a scripted scenario.

criterion.description: The goal, as the simulation's `success:` words it.

verdict.description: `none`: the run decided nothing about the goal.

allowed.description: Whether hosted evals are on and the organization's restrictions allow it to create runs and publish bundles. Region support, scenario checks, spend limits and a session's own conversation are still checked.

reason.description: The first restriction that applies, in this order. Null when allowed.

message.description: The restriction, in words to show a person. Null when allowed.

enabled.description: Whether hosted evals are on, whatever the organization's restrictions.

bundles.description: Whether stored bundles can be published here. False when that couldn't be established right now. The organization's restrictions are in `creation`.

suites.description: Whether suite runs can be created here. A suite run of a stored revision needs nothing more; one of inline `files` also needs `bundles`, to check them. The agent's region still checks each suite run's plan.

state.description: `available` means the kind is offered, not a promise of free capacity or a successful run. `unknown` means availability couldn't be established right now.

reason.description: Why the kind isn't available. Null when it is.

message.description: The reason, in words to show a person. Null when available.

audio.description: Whether synthetic runs of audio scenarios are offered, for every combination of caller and judge modality. When absent, treat it as `unknown`. It doesn't establish that the agent's own transport supports audio: that is checked when a run starts.

EvalBundleFiles.description: The bundle's files, as text, keyed by path relative to its root, and stored exactly as received: at least one, at most 2,000 files and 256 KiB of UTF-8 in all, at most 3.5 MiB as JSON (paths included, and 2 bytes more for each file), and the request at most 3 MiB of JSON. A path is a relative POSIX path of 1 to 1024 characters, with no NUL or backslash, not starting with `/`, with no empty, `.` or `..` segment, and not `__proto__`. No text may hold a NUL or an unpaired surrogate. Key order means nothing: answers list the files in code point order.

requestId.description: A UUID you generate for this request and send again, unchanged, when you retry it. Unique in the organization among publications.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting and ending with a letter or a digit. Unique among the organization's bundles.

bundleId.description: Null for an anonymous revision, which belongs to no bundle.

number.description: 1 for a bundle's first revision, one more for each after. Null for an anonymous revision.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of `{"formatVersion": 1, "files": files}`. It identifies the files, not whether they are valid.

coverage.description: How far the check went. `full`: Pipecat's scenario loader read every script and simulation. `structural`: the hosted-run rules and limits were checked without the loader, so a scenario the loader refuses can still pass, and is refused when it runs. `selection`: an anonymous revision's, checked for the scenarios its run selects.

EvalBundleChecker.description: What checked the revision, and the keys the check found would have no effect. Null for an anonymous revision.

build.description: The build of the eval service that checked it, when reported.

policyVersion.description: The version of the hosted-run rules it was checked against.

harnessVersion.description: The Pipecat version that checked it.

harnessCommit.description: The Pipecat commit that checked it, when that Pipecat was installed from source.

ignored.description: The first 20 keys that a run of a scenario would ignore.

key.description: A dotted path within the scenario, such as `user.voice`.

ignoredTotal.description: How many keys would be ignored in all.

bundleDeletedAt.description: When its bundle was deleted. Null while the bundle exists, and for an anonymous revision.

catalog.description: What the files hold, as the check classified them. `suites`: each suite file's `path`, `concurrency`, `repeat` and `entries`, each entry with its `label`, `runner_body`, `concurrency` and `selections` (`path` and `name`). `scenarioFiles`: each scenario file's scenarios, with their `name` and `kind` (`script`, `simulation`, or `rubric` for one of only `success:` and judged metrics, which no suite runs), and a simulation's `runs`. `fragments`: the files only includes read. `bodies`: each entry body file, by path. Null for an anonymous revision. Arrays keep their order; object keys are in code point order.

files.description: The files exactly as they were received, keyed in code point order.

updatedAt.description: When its latest revision was published.

deletedAt.description: When it was deleted. Null for every bundle listed or read; set only where a retried publication answers with a bundle deleted since.

problems.description: The first 50 problems: the bundle's own first, then by file.

total.description: How many problems there were, shown or not.

file.description: The file's path as sent, or null for the bundle as a whole.

scenario.description: The scenario's name, for a problem with one.

field.description: A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the file as parsed.

code.description: Why, such as `orphan_fragment`, `scenario_refused`, `suite_invalid` or `body_reserved_key` (a body holding a `__proto__` key, at any depth). Treat a code you don't know as a refusal too.

message.description: The problem, in words for a person. It names the file and numbers lists from 1.

EvalSuiteRunStatus.description: Live: `queued` (no member admitted yet), `running`. Ended: `completed` (every member admitted and ended), `cancelled`, `expired` (its deadline passed), `error` (see `error`).

EvalSuiteRunTarget.description: What a suite run runs, as accepted: a suite file of its revision's (`kind: suite`), or one scenario file as a suite of one entry (`kind: scenarios`), with the scenarios `scenarioNames` chose when the request named some.

EvalSuiteRunFilters.description: The request's filters, as accepted; null when it had none.

EvalSuiteRunCreateRequest.description: Exactly one of `bundleRevisionId` and `files` (the request's own, as an inline run's, checked as a bundle); and exactly one of `suitePath` and `scenarioPath`.

requestId.description: A UUID you generate for this request and send again, unchanged, when you retry it.

bundleRevisionId.description: A revision of one of the organization's bundles.

scenarioPath.description: A scenario file to run as a suite of one unlabelled entry: its scenarios except rubrics, or those `scenarioNames` lists.

scenarioNames.description: With `scenarioPath`: the scenarios to run, in this order, each named once.

filters.description: Narrows the plan before repetition. Each scenario named must be one the plan selects.

repeat.description: How many times every selected scenario runs, replacing the suite's `repeat:` and each simulation's `runs:`. Above 1, the suite run is a measurement, which reports pass rates instead of a verdict.

concurrency.description: How many members run at once, replacing the suite's `concurrency:`. An entry's own `concurrency:` still caps that entry.

deadlineSeconds.description: How long the suite run has from its acceptance, queueing and every member included: at most 12 hours, and 12 hours by default.

EvalSuitePlanRefusal.description: Why no plan could be made, by `kind`, with what it names: `suite_not_found` and `scenario_file_not_found` (`path`); `scenario_not_found`, `scenario_not_runnable` (a rubric), `scenario_named_twice` and `filter_not_in_plan` (`path`, `name`); `repeat_too_large` (`repeat`, `max`); `concurrency_too_large` (`concurrency`, `max`); `too_many_members` (`members`, `max`); `empty_plan`; and `plan_too_large` (`part`, `request` or `entries`, with `bytes` and `maxBytes`), more than a suite run can store. Treat a kind you don't know as a refusal too.

fingerprint.description: The judging version of these runs when the suite run is `mixed`. Null otherwise.

withoutVerdict.description: Ended runs without a verdict, counted in no rate.

passRate.description: `passed / (passed + failed + skipped)`. Null before any of those.

region.description: The agent's region, where its members run.

bundleRevisionId.description: The revision whose files it runs: the one its request named, or the anonymous revision its inline files were kept as.

measurement.description: Whether its `repeat` is above 1, set by the request or the suite file. A measurement reports pass rates rather than a verdict.

label.description: The entry's `name:`, or `""` when it has none.

concurrency.description: The entry's own cap on members at once. Null when it sets none.

body.description: Set when the entry gives its sessions a body, with the body file's `path` when it names one. The body itself is never shown. Null when it gives none.

counts.description: Its members by where they are. `pending`, `live` and `terminal` add up to `planned`; `passed`, `failed`, `skipped` and `withoutVerdict` add up to `terminal`.

pending.description: Not yet admitted. 0 once it has stopped or ended.

terminal.description: Ended, or never to be admitted now that it has stopped or ended.

withoutVerdict.description: Ended without a verdict (an error, not started, cancelled, expired), or never admitted.

verdict.description: Set once it has `completed`: `failed` if any member failed; otherwise null if any ended without a verdict; otherwise `passed` if any passed, and `skipped` if every one was skipped. Null while it runs, when it ended any other way, and for a measurement. A mixed suite run keeps its verdict.

passRates.description: A measurement's pass rates, by entry and scenario in plan order, and also by judging version when it is `mixed`. Null for any other suite run, and in lists: read the suite run for its own.

cancelRequestedAt.description: When its cancel was first requested. Null if never.

fingerprint.description: The judging version its members are held to, taken from the first member to report one. Null until one has.

mixed.description: Its members with a verdict were judged by more than one judging version: the platform's judging changed during the suite run, and some member couldn't be judged by the suite run's version in time. Its pass rates are then split by version.

startedAt.description: When its first member was admitted. Null before then.

EvalSuiteRunError.description: Why a suite run ended as `error`. Null on any other. `deployment_changed`: the agent's active deployment changed during it, naming the deployment it was accepted on (`expectedDeploymentId`), the one found instead (`deploymentId`), and the member whose session ran on it (`memberOrdinal`, null when the change was found before a member was admitted). `deployment_unknown`: which deployment a member's session ran on couldn't be confirmed. `revision_unavailable`: its bundle revision is no longer available.

EvalSuiteRunLimit.description: What the request asked for, what the suite file says, and what applies. Each is null when not set.

ordinal.description: Its place in the plan, from 0: the eval run's `suiteMemberOrdinal`.

entry.description: Its entry's index in the suite run's `entries`.

attempt.description: Which repetition of its scenario it is, from 1.

evalRunId.description: Its eval run, once it has been admitted. Null until then, and for a member never admitted.

SessionId.name: sessionId
SessionId.description: Session ID returned from the start endpoint

Path.name: path
Path.description: The endpoint path defined in your bot using the `@app` decorator

RevisionId.name: revisionId
RevisionId.description: ID of the eval bundle revision

SuiteRunId.name: suiteRunId
SuiteRunId.description: ID of the eval suite run

example.error: Attempt to start agent when deployment is not in ready state. Is your image pull secret valid?
Internal server error. Please check logs for more information or contact support.

BotResponseFailed.description: Pipecat Cloud couldn't get a usable response from your bot: the bot couldn't be reached, its response couldn't be read, or it sent a redirect that isn't followed. Can also be your bot's own `502`, passed through unchanged with its own body

error.description: Error message describing what went wrong

RegionUnavailable.description: The region hosting the agent can't be reached right now. Retry after the delay in the `Retry-After` header. Can also be your bot's own `503`, passed through unchanged with its own body and headers

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Added by Pipecat Cloud only when the region can't be reached

error.description: Error message describing what went wrong

code.description: Error code for programmatic handling, when present

example.error: Region 'us-west' is not reachable right now. Please retry shortly.

AgentTimeout.description: Your bot didn't respond before the request timed out. Can also be your bot's own `504`, passed through unchanged with its own body

error.description: Error message describing what went wrong

code.description: Error code for programmatic handling, when present

example.error: The agent did not respond before the request timed out.

EvalUnauthorized.description: Authentication is missing or invalid, or the user is not a member of the organization.

EvalInvalidQuery.description: A query parameter is invalid (`err.issues` says which).

EvalsDisabled.description: Hosted evals are not enabled here (code `EVALS-NOT-AVAILABLE`, no `Retry-After`).

EvalSuitesDisabled.description: Hosted evals are not enabled here (code `EVALS-NOT-AVAILABLE`), or suite runs aren't available here (code `EVAL-SUITES-NOT-AVAILABLE`). Neither has a `Retry-After`.

EvalBundleRefused.description: The body is invalid (`err.issues` says where), or the bundle's check refused it (code `EVAL-BUNDLE-REFUSED`, with `problems` and `total`).

EvalBundlePublishForbidden.description: The organization is suspended (code `PCC-1007`) or has HIPAA controls (code `EVALS-HIPAA-CONTROLS`). Its bundles can still be read and deleted.

EvalBundleTooLarge.description: The bundle holds more than 2,000 files or 256 KiB of UTF-8 in all, takes more than 3.5 MiB as JSON (paths included, and 2 bytes more for each file), or the request is more than 3 MiB of JSON; or what its files hold is too large to catalogue.

EvalBundleCheckUnavailable.description: The bundle couldn't be checked right now (code `503`; retry after the `Retry-After` header). Or, with no `Retry-After`: publishing bundles isn't available here (code `EVAL-BUNDLES-NOT-AVAILABLE`), or hosted evals are not enabled (code `EVALS-NOT-AVAILABLE`).
